note: Decoder-side hypotheses that were investigated and REJECTED: a cause that turned out not to be the cause, or a fix that was written, tested and reverted. The sibling ledger runtime-revision-assessments.json covers the other class, where the answer is a property of the compiler rather than of our code; a pattern that is unwitnessable by our oracle belongs there, not here. The point of both is that a rejected hypothesis is expensive evidence and is otherwise lost the moment a session ends -- PLAN.md records them chronologically, and this is the deduplicated index into it. An entry earns its place by saying what was tried, what killed it, and what a re-attempt should do instead.

hypotheses.title: Let the inline-IF guard skip address-less spliced DO headers
hypotheses.hypothesis: cal.exe emits a LOOP inside an inline IF because _fold_if's inline guard -- the leg that unfolds an IfInline containing a loop closer back into a guard plus body -- declines when the next statement is a codeless DO spliced in for the FOLLOWING loop, which carries no address. Teaching it to skip such headers, as the ELSE leg already does with else_stop, should let the unfold fire.
negative_evidence: The premise is correct and was confirmed by instrumentation: of cal's four IfInline-with-loop-closer regions, i=383/2032/2097 have a real next address and unfold, and only i=2007 has next_type=Do next_addr=None.

The fix nonetheless produces WRONG source. cal's bytes run input at 0x14c61, fstp BD at 0x14c6b, then the compare at 0x14c72, but the emitted result becomes `IF BD >= 1 AND BD <= 80 THEN <exit>` FOLLOWED BY the INPUT -- testing a stale BD before reading it.
It also fixes nothing: recompiling the result through the oracle fails with the SAME Error 435 at the same line.
The full suite passed and a block-nesting sweep called cal clean, so neither signal detected either failure.
hypotheses.instead: The defect is upstream of the guard. The recorded IfInline is addressed 0x14c72 but its body holds the Input from 0x14c61 -- a statement preceding its own address -- so the region absorbed the statement before it. Instrument whatever builds that region rather than repairing its consumers.
hypotheses.source: session 2026-07-30; commit ed78a4f is the unrelated fix that shipped from the same session

hypotheses.title: Six candidate source spellings for cal.exe's failing loop
hypotheses.hypothesis: cal's mis-folded loop can be reproduced by authoring the source shape it appears to have come from, giving a minimal fixture to calibrate against.
negative_evidence: All six compiled clean through the oracle and DECODE CORRECTLY today, so none reproduces the defect: compound integer tail test (LOOP WHILE A% < 1 OR A% > 80); the same with a single-precision variable; IF ... THEN BEEP ELSE EXIT LOOP inside a DO; IF ... AND ... THEN EXIT LOOP followed by BEEP; two such loops adjacent, the second starting at the first's exit address; and an external IF x THEN <line> jumping into the loop body.
hypotheses.instead: Stop guessing at the source. The trigger is not any of the obvious spellings, and four rounds of guessing cost more than the instrumentation that finally localized it.

hypotheses.title: Static-array grid offset is align16(scalar band width)
signatures: DGROUP layout not solvable from the calibrated rules
hypotheses.hypothesis: The array grid starts align16(scalar_band_width) past VAR_BASE, fitting three probe widths (38, 48, 62 -> 48, 48, 64) exactly.
negative_evidence: All three data points shared n_static=10, so the fit was unconstrained. An n=11 probe gave 32/48/32 bytes at n=9/10/11 -- not a function of width at all.

The real mechanism is not a formula: the compiler stamps a self-describing ordinary-scalars band descriptor into the init image, and the record run floats past variable-length init data by up to 720 bytes.
hypotheses.instead: When an offset refuses to fit a formula, hexdump the region and look for self-describing structure before curve-fitting. Two sessions of fitting were answered by one 30-line hexdump.

hypotheses.title: OR-flavored value-folded groups, (A AND B) OR (C OR D)
hypotheses.hypothesis: The mixed-precedence compound-IF folder can be extended to the OR-of-groups shape these four files need.
negative_evidence: Tried and reverted within the campaign; no fixture landed and the tree was confirmed clean afterwards.

A probe named q_orofors3.bas is recorded as reproducing the shape, so the gap is real -- what failed was the fix, not the diagnosis. NOTE the probe itself was never committed to wild/probes, so that evidence cannot currently be re-run and would have to be re-authored.
hypotheses.instead: Re-read PLAN.md:1775 before re-attempting; the entry says why the first attempt was abandoned.

hypotheses.title: LOCAL slot reuse across a FOR loop's scratch temps
hypotheses.hypothesis: The failure is a bad LOCAL frame bound.
negative_evidence: Traced precisely with an instrumented core.py, reverted and never committed: the variable-limit-FOR branch reserves a step/limit word pair that COLLIDES with a declared LOCAL. The frame bound is right; the reservation is what overlaps.
hypotheses.instead: Fix the reservation, not the bound.

hypotheses.title: emit_split cuts DO/LOOP and FOR/NEXT across $INCLUDE boundaries
hypotheses.hypothesis: Oversized programs emit as a root plus $INCLUDE files, and the split is by size rather than by block structure, so a DO or FOR can open in one include and close in the next -- which would explain the block-structure compile errors on exactly the programs large enough to be split.
negative_evidence: The imbalance is real: STATE001.INC has FOR=29 NEXT=27 and STATE003.INC has a NEXT with no FOR; INV87001/2/3 are unbalanced in both directions.
But TB's $INCLUDE is TEXTUAL, so a block may span files -- inv87.exe and invoice.exe compile successfully (delta -16) with badly unbalanced includes. That is proof, not inference.
cal.exe, which does NOT compile, is balanced within every include.
hypotheses.instead: Do not block-align the splitter. Per-include balance is neither necessary nor sufficient, and the compile errors on these programs have other causes.

hypotheses.title: A block-nesting sweep can stand in for the oracle on wild source
hypotheses.hypothesis: A cheap depth-counting check over emitted source can decide whether a wild program's structure is right, saving the minutes an oracle compile costs.
negative_evidence: False positives: it flags colon-joined single-line blocks (`FOR C = 1 TO 9: PRINT: NEXT C` in vhfprop) because it never splits on ':'.
False NEGATIVES, which is worse: it called cal.exe clean -- all six DO/LOOP pairs nesting at depth 1, final depth 0, no colon-joined closers -- while TB still rejected the file with Error 435.
It cannot model what TB actually validates, which includes at least the block level of a line-number jump target.
hypotheses.instead: Use it to FIND candidates and never as evidence a decode is right. The oracle byte compare is the only acceptance test, which is now written into CLAUDE.md.

hypotheses.title: TB rejects an IF..THEN <line> that jumps into a DO...LOOP body
hypotheses.hypothesis: cal.exe's remaining Error 435 comes from `IF BD >= 1 AND BD <= 80 THEN 20295` jumping from outside into the NEXT loop's body, which TB would reject as a block-level violation.
negative_evidence: Refuted by probe q_gotointoloop.bas: a DO/LOOP whose body is entered by an `IF c THEN <line>` from before the loop compiles clean through the oracle.
The real cause is elsewhere -- see the cal entry under 'Diagnosed but not landed' in STATUS.md: two EXIT LOOP statements stand outside any DO...LOOP.
hypotheses.instead: A jump into a block body is legal; do not spend time making the emitter avoid it. Check block MEMBERSHIP of EXIT statements instead.

hypotheses.title: Turbo Basic folds a byte-constant OUT into MOV AL,imm; OUT imm8,AL
hypotheses.hypothesis: The `b0 <val> e6 <port>` pairs filling wild zip.exe's and ziptest.exe's per-setting procedures are an OUT statement whose port and value both fit a byte, which Turbo Basic compiles to a compact MOV AL,value; OUT port,AL instead of the general mov-AX / mov-DX / OUT-DX form. scan.py's `out_imm` op and tests/tbx/test_out_immediate.py were both written on this premise.
negative_evidence: Refuted by oracle-compiled probes that all emit the GENERAL form and zero `b0/e6` bytes: wild/probes/probe_out_const_toplevel.bas (`OUT 67, 116` at top level, the exact port/value pair zip uses), wild/probes/probe_out_const_in_sub.bas (the same three OUTs inside a SUB, matching the shape in zip), and a DEF SEG + hex-literal variant. Turbo Basic 1.1 has no byte-constant OUT template; INP and OUT always route the port through DX (EC/EE).

The mapping was never calibrated: `out_imm` had no compiled fixture. t1_out.bas uses port 888 (>255) and t1_out2.bas a variable operand, so neither exercised it, and test_out_immediate.py asserted only the scanner's behaviour on hand-built bytes plus that zip decodes -- it never recompiled anything.

wild/probes/probe_inline_out_imm.bas shows what DOES produce those bytes: a `SUB name INLINE` with a `$INLINE &HB0,&H74,&HE6,&H43,...` list. The bodies are `55 8b ec` + 12 raw port bytes + `5d cb`, i.e. a $INLINE list carrying its own bp frame, with Turbo Basic appending the terminating CB (the skip-jmp spans 17 = 16 list bytes + 1).

What the code actually does, which the old `out_imm` comment got wrong by calling these 'tone' procedures: command byte 74h to port 43h selects PIT counter 1, mode 2, 16-bit binary, then a divisor goes to counter 1's data port 41h. Counter 1 is the DRAM refresh request generator, not the speaker (counter 2, port 42h) and not the system tick (counter 0, port 40h). zip.exe writes 26 such procedures to ZIPA.BIN..ZIPZ.BIN, one per divisor -- 9/12/15/18 then 30..240 by tens, against a stock IBM value of 18 -- so raising the divisor cuts refresh bursts and steals fewer bus cycles. It is a PC speed-up utility; ziptest.exe carries the 23 settings from 18 upward and probes how far the machine's RAM tolerates it.

Cost of the false mapping, measured through the oracle: emitting `OUT p, v` recompiles to the general form, so zip.exe grew +592 bytes (78 OUTs) and ziptest.exe +224 (69). They were the two least-identical comparable programs in the corpus (96.9% and 93.2%) entirely because of this.
hypotheses.instead: Do not look for an OUT spelling that reproduces these bytes -- none exists. The bodies are source-level `SUB name INLINE` + `$INLINE`, which `ir.Inline` and emit0 already round-trip byte-exactly. FIXED the same session: `out_imm` is gone and `_try_inline_rescue` now claims a framed `55 8b ec ... 5d cb` body when its CONTENT holds an instruction sequence the compiler cannot emit -- currently `mov al,imm8; out imm8,al`, extensible as further such sequences are proved. Match whole sequences, never a bare opcode-range test: these bodies are not disassembled, and searching the E4-E7 port-I/O range accepted `89 e5`, the alternate `mov bp,sp`, in the prologue of the framed procedures the guard exists to reject (wild CVT2TB.EXE, phone.exe, which stay fail-loud). The check is one-way -- it only rules a body IN. Fixture t1_inlineport; zip.exe 96.87% -> 98.75% identical (delta +592 -> +64), ziptest.exe 93.17% -> 98.97% (+224 -> -224).
